Title: Safe Passage
Premise_Logline: The family calls in the passage debt she has owed since she was nineteen: move one man to the border — the same man they never intend to let arrive.
A_Plot: A runs the ordered passage, works out mid-route that the delivery is a disposal, and tries to land B alive without forfeiting the people she has quietly moved before him.
B_Plot: The private list of eleven people A has moved off the family's books becomes D's leverage the moment she deviates from the route.

Mandatory_Set_Pieces_with_Phase.beat: the passage debt is called in at the yard: A is handed B and a fixed route
first deviation: A takes an unlisted crossing and loses the family's eyes
freighter layover: A and B trade the truth about what the delivery is
consent negotiation before first C3 contact
the handover at the border yard resolves on the page

Antagonistic_Force.name: D
Antagonistic_Force.descriptor: the family's road boss; holds both the passage debt and the disposal order

Allies_Confidants.name: C
Allies_Confidants.descriptor: A's yard mechanic and dispatcher; the only other person who knows the unlisted routes

Continuity_Constraints: the ledger case from Book One is closed and public; every party knows the family is being watched
A owes the passage debt from Book One; it is called in on story day 1 and cannot be transferred
the route is physical and continuous - no scene relocates the pair without an on-page leg
B's federal testimony date is fixed at story day 19 and never moves
A and D are never in the same room until Phase 6

Sentence_Rhythm_Targets.punctuation_habits: terse periods; sparse em dash; no semicolons in dialogue

Signature_Moves: distance and fuel math surfacing under emotional load
doors and exits counted on entry

hard_no: sexual coercion as a route to intimacy between the leads
handled_off_page: the relocation details of B's family
Taboo_List_and_Sensitive_Notes.notes: All intimacy is consent-gated by the 4.5 architecture. The custody imbalance between A and B is named on the page and never used as a route to contact; coercion pressure runs through D and the debt.

Redundancy_Rules.note: tightens the Ph4-5 default window of 2; windows may tighten, never loosen

Hook_Line: She owes the family one passage. They just handed her the man they never intend to let arrive.
Blurb_Draft: I have moved people the family wanted gone and people the family never knew existed, and I have never once asked which was which. That is the price of the passage they bought me at nineteen, and this week they came to collect it. One man. One route. Nineteen days to the border, and orders not to deviate. Except the man in my passenger seat is a federal witness with a date in court, the route runs through three yards where nobody expects him to arrive breathing, and somewhere between the lake and the line I stopped counting him as cargo. I can deliver him or I can keep him. There is no manifest for both.
City_Or_Region: Chicago to the Michigan lakeshore and the Ontario border
Locale_Signature: a truck yard's sodium lights burning through lake fog
the long grey seam where the freighter channel meets the breakwater
Occupation_Primary_A: owner-operator of a small freight and courier yard
Goal_External_A: discharge the passage debt and get the yard out from under the family
Goal_Internal_A: to stop being something that is owed
Wound_A: her own passage was bought for her at nineteen, priced without her consent, and never written off
Flaw_A: routes people instead of knowing them - it is how she keeps them alive and how she keeps them at distance
Secret_A: she has moved eleven people off the family's books and kept the list
Backstory_A: Brought into the country at nineteen on a passage the family arranged and priced; built a legitimate yard on the proceeds of illegitimate routes; has spent a decade paying interest on a favor she never agreed to.
Physical_Description_A: Short and weather-worn; hands scarred from cargo straps; hair cut to stay out of the way; a coat she can sleep in.
Voice_Verbal_Tic_A: gives distances and arrival times where a feeling was asked for
Body_Language_Default_A: checks the mirrors and the exits before she answers
Fear_Profile_A: the list being found; owing again; arriving somewhere with no way back out
Occupation_Primary_B: former transport foreman for the family
Occupation_Secondary_B: federal witness under a protective agreement
Goal_Internal_B: to be known by one person who understands exactly what he was
Wound_B: he drove the family's routes for eleven years without asking what the cargo was, and once it was a person
Flaw_B: confesses to be absolved rather than to be known
Secret_B: he recognises the yard - he routed A's own passage at nineteen
Backstory_B: Raised inside the family's transport arm and given its routes at twenty-three; walked into a federal office the week after a delivery he could not stop replaying.
Physical_Description_B: Tall, thinned out by six months of waiting; a driver's tan that stops at the wrist.
Voice_Verbal_Tic_B: says what he did before he says why
Body_Language_Default_B: sits where he can see the road behind them
Fear_Profile_B: dying before the record exists; being remembered only as what he drove
Subplot_A: C's yard licence is the collateral D threatens the first time A leaves the route
Subplot_B: the eleven names on A's private list surface one at a time as the family audits her routes
Cover_Cue_Main: woman at the open door of a freight truck, back to camera, headlights behind her
Cover_Cue_Background: lake fog over a night truck yard, sodium lights
Back_Cover_Copy: She owes the family one passage, and the family has finally named it: one man, one route, no deviations. Nineteen days to the border. Nineteen days to decide whether she is the delivery or the last thing standing between him and the water.
Dedication_Line: For everyone still paying off a road they never chose.
Content_Warnings_Public: coercion and threats by third parties
